annotations.text:
BOTH ARTBOARDS ARE WORKING PROTOTYPES — click them.

LEFT: the home screen. The dark strip on top is preview scaffolding, not a shipped feature — click a chip and the whole screen re-skins. Palette, plaque shape, corner radius, shadow language and the ambient effect all change together: confetti on Slot Machine, neon flicker on Neon, felt shimmer on Tropical, none on Terminal Classic.

RIGHT: Admin. PIN is 2468 — try a wrong one first. Once in, pick a theme and press Apply; the admin chrome itself re-skins to whatever is live.

HOW IT WORKS — 83 CSS custom properties, defined four times over as [data-theme="terminal" | "slot" | "neon" | "tropical"]. Switching sets one attribute on the root; a 240ms transition carries the change. Every colour in the page resolves through a var(), so this is the real implementation architecture, not a mockup of one.

Theme is a single global setting — settings/site.theme in Firestore, read with onSnapshot, so a change reaches every open phone without a reload. The PIN gate is a deterrent against accidental changes, not a security boundary: it is checked in the browser and anyone can read it in the page source. That is proportionate, since anyone with the link can already edit the scores themselves.
